reviews.review:
Updated Review: First disclaimer - I had to look all over the discussion board to try more than 6 different methods to get the Risk of Rian (2013) to work. Prior to this I was loosing all progress and the game wasn't loading correctly.

The game is super enjoyable when your able to play; By now many of you understand the concept behind the game. Run around, loot/collect, spend currency, then beat each level, etc.. Being that it's 2026 I can see why this game had such a large following. It's truly a classic and should be attempted by individuals who like the roguelike action genre.

Controls: 
They are super iffy you can only attack in the direction you are facing, there is no real default mouse support. But thankfully on the discussion boards I found a keyboard layout that works for me. that being said yes the controls are a bit outdated.

Screen Visual: 
In the trailer what you are seeing is zoomed in 2 and 3, the truth is you start playing the game with a default setting where your character is probably the size of a Zero with a 12 point font. This allows you to view the sooo much more of the map you are on so you can semi figure out your route. I think once you memorize more of the stages this probably is used less. BUT! my issue is zoom 2 & 3 are way too strong, I don't understand why zoom 2 has to go in soo much there should have been a scrolling adjustor for your zoom in options. SO again be aware that you'll start off in ant view mode.

Characters/Items: 
I've hardly unlocked anything after 9.6hours granted 5 hours was erased due to the first thing I mentioned in this review. All characters besides your starting character are locked behind unlocks so what does this mean to you. This means you may never play any more than 3 characters maybe 5 before you quit the game. The same is true for items as well you may never play with but half or less of the items before you stop playing the game.

Movement/Mobility:
Maybe it's because I'm a noob but movement or mobility just feels limited with the characters especially as a noob. That's all, i just wish there were a bit more iframes... The game is designed around higher level of game play.
Difficulty Settings:
Honestly I have the same issue with RoR2 the easiest difficulty is too easy and unlocks don't save. The "Normal" difficulty is just slightly to hard for many of us. Just like the zooming function there needed to be an inbetween and that would hit the sweet spot for many people (assuming) 

conclusion good game, I would've loved this even more so back in 2013. Get it, try it out, work with what it presents to you.

this game is amazing and is really time consuming i would 100% recommend if you like games like this ones that take some time and memory to gt the hang of but once you do its basically smooth sailing from there, the things you can do and that fact that you can play with friends makes it just that much better thres even bosses just for you and your friends utter peak would but again and would buy again after that

I've felt conflicted in my attempts to try to get into Risk of Rain over the years. It has a really beautiful soundtrack and the sort of visuals that would be right up my alley, however these were not enough to carry otherwise lackluster gameplay.

The main way of fighting enemies is to run away from them constantly, only turning around to fire at them when an ability recharges, then either continuing to run or dodge through them to run the other way instead. There is also an in-game timer that makes enemies spawn more frequently and with more HP as time goes on, which makes it so going fast is encouraged. If too much time is taken the game then becomes a Sisyphean task of having to run away, turn to shoot, repeat as enemies take actual ages to kill.

I feel the timer was added in part because if it wasn't there, the optimal strategy would be to just whittle enemies health down while running away for as long as possible. This gets to the main point of my issue, in which I can't help but feel difficulty is artificially inflated as a cover for how unengaging the combat actually is. Every few years I would try Risk of Rain again and drop it after a run or two as I never felt challenged in the right way.

While I was open to the idea of playing the whole game through to properly judge it in its entirety rather than just the early game, upon trying to launch Risk of Rain in 2026 I was informed I had to accept a EULA for a game I've already owned for nearly a decade already, with a lot of clauses that are unfriendly to the consumer, thus killing any incentive left I had to trying this series again.
